newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: GOLF-Scahill qualifies for European golf tour.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-Scahill qualifies for European golf tour.

text.p: There was more success for New Zealand golf with Wellington professional Stephen Scahill winning a prized European golf tour card for next season in the last qualifying event.
His 13-under 275 in Portugal's UAP Grand Final moved Scahill from 16th -- one spot outside the qualifying mark -- to 13th.
In doing so New Zealand, for the first time, will have four players contesting the European Tour next season.
Scahill will join his fellow Eisenhower Trophy winning team-mate Michael Campbell, plus Frank Nobilo and Greg Turner on the tour.
Today's fourth place after rounds of 70 67 69 and 69 lifted Scahill's challenge tour earnings to $61,000.
New Zealand Golf Association chief executive Grant Clements said that for Scahill today's result would have been like winning the British Open.
"It was a result which will affect the rest of his life. He would have known that playing the final round. It is a really gutsy effort," Clements said.
Clements maintains Scahill has the game to go to the top.

"The hardest thing to do over there is to qualify. People don't realise how difficult it is being on the other side of the world. It is difficult to get over there and then overcome the insurmountable odds," he said.
"The local players can live at home in Europe which makes it very easy for them. Players like Stephen have to go to Europe, find somewhere to live and overcome everything that goes with that.
"You have to take your hat off to him."

Clements said New Zealand would have to work to get even more players into Europe. Another member of the successful 1992 Eisenhower team Grant Moorhead was also about to embark on a European qualifying mission, Clements said.
